content: 1. Didanosine chewable tablets and oral solution should be administered either 2 hours before or several hours after moxifloxacin administration to avoid interaction. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Moxifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. An alternative or additional form of birth control may be necessary during concurrent use. 3. Moxifloxacin can increase the risk of central nervous system (CNS) stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 4. Moxifloxacin increases the levels or effects of digoxin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Moxifloxacin and disopyramide both prolong the QTc interval, making their concurrent use contraindicated due to the risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 6. Moxifloxacin and dofetilide both increase the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 7. Moxifloxacin and dolasetron both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 8. Moxifloxacin and donepezil both increase the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 9. Moxifloxacin and doxepin both prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 10. Moxifloxacin and dronedarone both increase the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 11. Moxifloxacin and droperidol both prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 12. Moxifloxacin and efavirenz both increase the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 13. Moxifloxacin and eliglustat both prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 14. Moxifloxacin and encorafenib both increase the QTc interval. Encorafenib is associated with dose-dependent QTc prolongation. Avoid coadministration with drugs known to prolong the QT interval. If unavoidable, close monitoring, including ECGs, is recommended. 15. Moxifloxacin and entrectinib both prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 16. Moxifloxacin and epinephrine both increase the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 17. Moxifloxacin and epinephrine racemic both prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 18. Moxifloxacin and eribulin both increase the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. If coadministration is necessary, ECG monitoring is recommended. 19. Moxifloxacin and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 20. Moxifloxacin and erythromycin ethylsuccinate both increase the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 21. Moxifloxacin and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 22. Moxifloxacin and erythromycin stearate both increase the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 23. Moxifloxacin and escitalopram both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 24. Moxifloxacin increases the levels of estazolam by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 25. Moxifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 26. Moxifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Moxifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of estropipate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 28. Moxifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Moxifloxacin decreases the effects of ethosuximide by an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 30. Moxifloxacin and etodolac increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 31. Moxifloxacin and etrasimod both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Etrasimod may transiently decrease heart rate and delay AV conduction when initiated. It may also increase the risk of QT prolongation and Torsades de Pointes when coadministered with Class Ia or Class III antiarrhythmic drugs or other QT-prolonging agents. 32. Moxifloxacin and ezogabine both increase toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Slight and transient QT prolongation has been observed with ezogabine, particularly at doses titrated to 1200 mg/day. QT interval monitoring is recommended when ezogabine is prescribed with QT-prolonging agents. 33. Fennel decreases the levels of moxifloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 34. Moxifloxacin and fenoprofen increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 35. Ferric citrate decreases the levels or effects of moxifloxacin by drug binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer moxifloxacin at least 2 hours before or after ferric citrate. Caution and monitoring are advised. 36. Ferric maltol decreases the levels of moxifloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 37. Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels of moxifloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 38. Ferrous gluconate decreases the levels of moxifloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 39. Ferrous sulfate decreases the levels of moxifloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 40. Moxifloxacin and fexinidazole both prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. Avoid coadministration of fexinidazole with drugs known to block potassium channels and/or prolong the QT interval. 41. Moxifloxacin and fingolimod both increase the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 42. Moxifloxacin and flecainide both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 43. Moxifloxacin and fluconazole both increase the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 44. Moxifloxacin and fludrocortisone increase the risk of tendon rupture when coadministered with corticosteroids. Caution and monitoring are advised. 45. Moxifloxacin and fluoxetine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 46. Moxifloxacin and fluphenazine both increase the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 47. Moxifloxacin increases the levels of flurazepam by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 48. Moxifloxacin and flurbiprofen increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 49. Moxifloxacin and fluvoxamine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 50. Moxifloxacin and formoterol both increase the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 51. Moxifloxacin and foscarnet both prolong the QTc interval. The mechanism is unknown. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. There is also a risk of tonic-clonic seizures. 52. Moxifloxacin decreases the effects of fosphenytoin by an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. There are also case reports of quinolones increasing phenytoin levels. 53. Moxifloxacin and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 54. Moxifloxacin and gadobenate both increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 55. Moxifloxacin and gemtuzumab both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 56. Moxifloxacin and gepirone both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 57. Moxifloxacin and gilteritinib both prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 58. Moxifloxacin and givinostat both increase the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs at initiation, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or if there is a change from baseline greater than 60 ms. 59. Moxifloxacin and glasdegib both prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for increased risk of QTc interval prolongation. 60. Moxifloxacin increases the effects of glimepiride by pharmacodynamic synergy. Caution and monitoring are advised. Quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperor hypoglycemia. Gatifloxacin is most likely to cause dysglycemia, while moxifloxacin is least likely. 61. Moxifloxacin increases the effects of glipizide by pharmacodynamic synergy. Caution and monitoring are advised. Quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperor hypoglycemia. Gatifloxacin is most likely to cause dysglycemia, while moxifloxacin is least likely. 62. Moxifloxacin increases the effects of glyburide by pharmacodynamic synergy. Caution and monitoring are advised. Quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperor hypoglycemia. Gatifloxacin is most likely to cause dysglycemia, while moxifloxacin is least likely. 63. Goserelin increases the toxicity of moxifloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. There is an increased risk of Torsades de Pointes. 64. Moxifloxacin and granisetron both prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 65. Moxifloxacin and haloperidol both increase the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 66. Histrelin increases the toxicity of moxifloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. There is an increased risk of Torsades de Pointes. 67. Moxifloxacin and hydrocortisone increase the risk of tendon rupture when coadministered with corticosteroids. Caution and monitoring are advised. 68. Moxifloxacin and hydrocortisone rectal increase the risk of tendon rupture when coadministered with corticosteroids. Caution and monitoring are advised. 69. Moxifloxacin and hydroxychloroquine sulfate both prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 70. Hydroxyzine increases the toxicity of moxifloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. There is an increased risk of Torsades de Pointes. 71. Moxifloxacin and ibuprofen increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 72. Moxifloxacin and ibuprofen IV increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 73. Moxifloxacin and ibutilide both prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use is contraindicated due to the risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 74. Moxifloxacin and iloperidone both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 75. Moxifloxacin and imipramine both prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 76. Moxifloxacin and indacaterol inhaled both increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Drugs known to prolong the QTc interval may increase the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 77. Moxifloxacin and indapamide both prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use is contraindicated due to the risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 78. Moxifloxacin and indomethacin increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 79. Moxifloxacin and inotuzumab both prolong the QTc interval. Their concurrent use should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs and electrolytes before and after initiation of any QTc-prolonging drug, and monitor periodically as clinically indicated during treatment. 80. Moxifloxacin increases the effects of insulin aspart by pharmacodynamic synergy. Caution and monitoring are advised. Quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperor hypoglycemia. Gatifloxacin is most likely to cause dysglycemia, while moxifloxacin is least likely. 81. Moxifloxacin increases the effects of insulin detemir by pharmacodynamic synergy. Caution and monitoring are advised. Quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperor hypoglycemia. Gatifloxacin is most likely to cause dysglycemia, while moxifloxacin is least likely. 82. Moxifloxacin increases the effects of insulin glargine by pharmacodynamic synergy. Caution and monitoring are advised. Quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperor hypoglycemia. Gatifloxacin is most likely to cause dysglycemia, while moxifloxacin is least likely. 83. Moxifloxacin increases the effects of insulin glulisine by pharmacodynamic synergy. Caution and monitoring are advised. Quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperor hypoglycemia. Gatifloxacin is most likely to cause dysglycemia, while moxifloxacin is least likely. 84. Moxifloxacin increases the effects of insulin lispro by pharmacodynamic synergy. Caution and monitoring are advised. Quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperor hypoglycemia. Gatifloxacin is most likely to cause dysglycemia, while moxifloxacin is least likely. 85. Moxifloxacin increases the effects of insulin NPH by pharmacodynamic synergy. Caution and monitoring are advised. Quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperor hypoglycemia. Gatifloxacin is most likely to cause dysglycemia, while moxifloxacin is least likely.
